caption:
Krishna Pragjyotishpur pahunche, Narakasur ka ant ab hoga.
Bhagavata Purana ki yeh katha batati hai ki bahari rakshas hi nahi, andar ke Narakasur ko bhi Krishna hi maarte hain.
Aapke andar ka Narakasur kaun hai — krodh, lobh, ya ahankaar?

Music: Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com), CC BY 4.0

claims.claim: Narakasura (Bhaumasura) was the king of Pragjyotishapura and son of Bhoodevi
Narakasura stole Aditi's earrings and kidnapped 16,000 women
Krishna, accompanied by Satyabhama, defeated Narakasura and Mura
The story appears in Bhagavata Purana 10th Canto, Chapter 59
claims.basis: Critical edition of Bhagavata Purana (Skandha 10, Adhyaya 59)

figures.name: Krishna
figures.look: Divine youth with radiant dark blue skin and an athletic build. He wears a peacock feather in a golden crown, a yellow silk dhoti with intricate gold embroidery, and ornate gold jewelry. A flute rests at his waist, and his expression remains calm and compassionate.

figures.name: Satyabhama
figures.look: Radiant queen with fair skin and a graceful build. She wears an elegant traditional silk saree in deep maroon with gold borders, adorned with ornate gold necklaces and bangles. Her expression is determined and compassionate, standing in a regal, upright posture.

figures.name: Narakasura
figures.look: Large demon king with dark skin, a muscular build, fierce red eyes, and sharp fangs. He wears ornate iron armor, a spiked crown, and carries multiple weapons in his hands. He maintains an aggressive, powerful stance, exuding a dark and formidable presence.

figures.name: Aditi
figures.look: Divine mother goddess with glowing fair skin and a gentle, serene face. She wears a simple white silk saree with golden trim and modest gold jewelry. Her posture is graceful, and her hands are held in a gesture of blessing and relief.

figures.name: Mura
figures.look: Fierce demon guardian with dark skin, a massive muscular build, and sharp horns. He wears heavy bronze armor and carries a large iron club. He maintains an intimidating, vigilant posture while standing guard at the massive palace gate.

figures.name: Bhoodevi
figures.look: Earth goddess with radiant skin and a gentle, maternal face. She wears a traditional silk saree in earthy tones, adorned with gold jewelry. Her expression is loving, and her hands are raised in a gesture of blessing toward her son.

figures.name: 16000 Women
figures.look: A large group of women with varied skin tones, wearing colorful silk sarees and ornate gold jewelry. They display expressions of relief and joy. They stand together in orderly rows, maintaining a graceful and hopeful posture.

places.name: Pragjyotishpur Palace
places.look: Massive stone architecture featuring high arched gates and intricate carvings of mythical creatures. The structure is decorated with warm gold and deep maroon accents, illuminated by soft divine light, remaining ornate yet uncluttered in design.

places.name: Dark Palace Hall
places.look: Dimly lit interior featuring stone pillars and deep shadows. A throne made of dark obsidian sits prominently, decorated with ornate carvings and deep maroon tapestries. Glowing embers provide light, creating a mysterious and epic atmosphere.

places.name: Palm-leaf manuscript
places.look: Ancient textured surface showing aged organic material. The background features soft golden light, warm gold and deep maroon decorative borders, and clear, elegant artistic space, maintaining an ornate but uncluttered aesthetic suitable for traditional storytelling.
